[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining. i see we've got the procurement and security folks on the line, appreciate you taking time. goal today is to run the preflight — legal + tech — so we can get pilot scoped and the MSA/DPA pathing clear.
[00:18] Karen (ODIN - Procurement): thanks, yes hi. timeline is tight: board asked for vendor approval before end of November. so we need commercial + legal ok then procurement will route to finance.
[00:29] Samir: got it, end of Nov. we can try to move fast. Emily — can you give a 3-minute tech overview for the team?
[00:36] Emily (Redwood SE): sure thanks. um, quick high level — Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC/on-prem installs. for PHI customers like ODIN — most folks choose Dedicated or Private depending on residency. our Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with SLA and isolated tenant network; Private gives customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem package.
[01:02] Dr. Alan Reeves (CTO): quick question — if we go Dedicated, does data ever leave our VPC? like egress to redwood control plane? we need to know where keys live.
[01:13] Emily: good call. with Dedicated the inference plane sits in our tenancy and we can integrate to your KMS — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations. control plane signals are minimal; we can offer a Private control plane for full separation. keys can be customer-managed so we do not hold plaintext keys. sometimes the transcript says K M S weirdly but that's the gist.
[01:36] Priya (Security): customer-managed KMS is a hard requirement for any live PHI. also need audit logs, RBAC, SAML SSO, and SOC2 type II evidence. will you provide encryption in transit + at rest specifics?
[01:50] Emily: yes — TLS 1.2/1.3, AES-256 at rest. we can provide encryption architecture doc and sample audit logs. our SOC2 pack includes control mappings.
[02:05] Jill (Legal): from a DPA perspective we have a few non-negotiables: data residency in US, subprocessors list, subprocessing notifications and breach timelines. also we typically redline MSA clauses on indemnity and liability caps.
[02:20] Samir: understood. we'll send a DPA + MSA with proposed language. to be efficient, can you prioritize which clauses are blockers vs negotiable?
[02:31] Jill: yes we'll send a redline priority list by Friday.
[02:34] Karen: one procurement-specific — pricing. we need cost projections: expected monthly inference tokens for pilot and for 6-12 month production. show both Hosted and Dedicated pricing, plus egress fees.
[02:49] Samir: sure will do. Emily, can you explain the cost vs latency trade — especially quantization and batch sizing options?
[02:57] Emily: yeah... so basically lower-cost quantized models give a slight hit in quality but major cost reductions. batching increases throughput and lowers per-token cost, but adds a small latency tail; continuous batching and prefix/KV cache can reduce token compute while preserving response time for cached contexts. for low-latency interactive flows we recommend smaller batch windows or a latency tier on Dedicated. we also do auto-fallback to cheaper variants when capacity's constrained.
[03:28] Marco (Platform Eng): how deterministic is latency on Dedicated? p95 targets? we need <200ms for certain flows.
[03:36] Emily: for short prompts on optimized kernels and proper instance type we regularly hit p95 ~120-180ms. longer contexts obviously increase. we'll run perf tests during pilot and provide the raw traces. note that perf varies by model, sequence length and hardware; we provide model cards with typical profiled numbers.
[03:58] Dr. Alan Reeves: what about egress — do you charge per GB leaving region? and do you support bringing your own key to prevent cloud-provider egress charges?
[04:10] Samir: egress charges depend on deployment mode. Hosted can have inter-region charges; Dedicated inside your cloud typically doesn't charge you extra from our side but cloud egress applies. for Private/on-prem we can avoid that. BYOK for keys is supported.
[04:25] Priya: one more security nuance: for PHI we need formal attestation of data handling and option for on-prem air-gapped deployment if required by audits. what's the standard path?
[04:38] Emily: we have an on-prem offering for regulated customers — it's a shipped package and we work with your infra team. it's more involved and will impact timeline, but possible. often customers start with Dedicated in a private VPC with customer-managed KMS, run an audit/pilot, then consider on-prem migration if required.
[04:58] Karen: timeline again — commercial signoff plus legal by EoN? can we get a sample SLA for Dedicated and Private?
[05:06] Samir: yes we'll attach the SLA, and the MSA/DPA. expect a draft MSA + DPA and pricing sheet in 48–72 hours.
[05:15] [Speaker 1]: (garbled) ... there was a question about backups and log retention windows...
[05:22] Priya: retention windows — for pilot we'll need 90 days of logs, but for production 7 years for audit artifacts; is that supported?
[05:32] Emily: yes we can export logs to your S3 or syslog with retention policies. retention is configurable; longer-term retention can be exported off-platform to your archive.
[05:42] Marco: how intrusive is the pilot? we want to avoid sending real PHI in initial runs; can we run synthetic datasets?
[05:50] Emily: absolutely — pilot can use synthetic data or subset anonymized data. we'll support the same telemetry and perf profiling without real PHI. also we can run privacy-preserving evals.
[06:01] Jill: legal question: liability cap — will Redwood accept our standard 1x annual fee cap?
[06:09] Samir: typical Redwood terms have higher caps for enterprise; open to discuss. we'll include both standard and escalated options in the term sheet for negotiation.
[06:18] Karen: procurement also needs references — do you have healthcare customers or attestation?
[06:24] Samir: yes we can share redacted references and a healthcare customer brief. we'll include a short case study and compliance attestations.
[06:31] Dr. Alan Reeves: for connectivity, we use private peering to our cloud; can Redwood route to our VPC endpoints?
[06:39] Emily: yes, with Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering, PrivateLink equivalents, and direct connect arrangements. we'll put the network checklist in the runbook.
[06:50] Karen: great. any blockers from Redwood side for a pilot starting Nov 17?
[06:55] Samir: not that I see. Emily will lead the tech validation and I will lead commercial and legal.
[07:02] Emily: i'll coordinate with Marco on the test harness and provide the perf matrix.
[07:07] Marco: ok will confirm resource availability.
[07:11] Samir: recap: we will send MSA + DPA draft, pricing sheet with hosted/dedicated/private scenarios, SOC2 pack and deployment diagram; ODIN will send DPA redline priorities and PHI scope. pilot target week starting 2025-11-17.
[07:26] Karen: sounds good thanks. last thing — any competitors we should know about in your view?
[07:31] Samir: customers sometimes evaluate Anthropic and Google Vertex; we'll highlight differentiation on production SLOs and Dedicated/private tooling.
[07:42] Jill: thanks everyone. we may loop in procurement counsel after redlines.
